### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **95** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, `packages/qa/scenarios/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`, `objectName (literal, 56 pages)`
- **53** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf781c2383720f9402a6355dac14b1692ef81b70` — the merge of head `4dd3edc52bdfe115b3b86dce74a3b31df4450e4a` into base `a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf781c2383720f9402a6355dac14b1692ef81b70 && git checkout cf781c2383720f9402a6355dac14b1692ef81b70
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4 4dd3edc52bdfe115b3b86dce74a3b31df4450e4a && git checkout -B drift-repro a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4 && git merge --no-ff 4dd3edc52bdfe115b3b86dce74a3b31df4450e4a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a2437b560bd8872feece6ec8b57c6fdf21cff1f4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review — PR #30594
Head-sha: 4dd3edc52bdfe115b3b86dce74a3b31df4450e4a
Verdict: **PASS**

This is the record of an isolated, read-only contract-tier reviewer the epic seat ran on this head (the seat posts it; the reviewer wrote nothing).

1. **The move preserves behaviour.** The move commit `e4279a2d` is pure renames: 11 files, 0 insertions and 0 deletions. After it, the source changes are rewiring only:
   - real schema types replace the mirrors (`ScenarioExpect`, `z.infer` of `OutcomeSchema` / `PostStateSchema`, `Truth`, a `Pick` of `ScenarioCard`);
   - `resolveStackCollection` comes from its owner `@objectstack/core`;
   - `measureChecks` is exported.

   No check body changed, and no assertion was weakened.
2. **CLI cleanup.** No scenario code and no mirrored types remain under `packages/cli`. `packages/cli/package.json` is unchanged. The `MetadataEvalCase` move into `corpus.ts` is `interface` / `import type` / `export type` only, so it emits no JS.
3. **Clause-② no.** There is no new `@objectstack/cli` entry export. `@objectstack/scenarios` stays `private: true`, and its `./score` subpath is a private-package entry. `src/index.ts` does not re-export it.
4. **Security pin.** The `second-object-read-exposure` row is re-keyed to `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-graph.ts`, with the same `not-a-served-read` class and the same reason, which is still true: it reads the artifact only, with no record, fetch or child_process.
5. **The changeset correction holds, judged sentence by sentence** (table below).
6. **CI on this head:** 70 check-runs. The only failures are `Check Changeset` ×2, the designed DELIBERATE CORRECTION red.

| # | Deleted `.changeset/30290-scenario-scorer-port.md` (pending, unreleased) | False after this PR? |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | `'@objectstack/cli': patch` as the scorer's bump | yes: the CLI no longer ships the scorer |
| O2 | "feat(cli): a deterministic scenario scorer under `src/lint` …" | yes: nothing scenario-related remains under `packages/cli/src/lint` |
| O3/O4 | `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` | still true; carried verbatim in the new note |
| O5/O7/O8 | Structural scorer / artifact reader / Run grader at `src/lint/scenario-*.ts` | yes as CLI notes: those paths are gone; the functions are unchanged in the moved modules |
| O6 | The two closed shape checks | yes as a CLI statement; the behaviour survives in the private package, never released |
| O9 | "… the `os lint --eval` wiring is a later change" | yes: cancelled by ruling D (comment 6670490510 on #30291) |

| # | New `.changeset/30291-scenario-tag-checks.md` | True? |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | `@objectstack/scenarios` and `@objectstack/cli` patch | yes |
| N2/N5–N7 | the scorer lives in `@objectstack/scenarios`; the private `./score` entry (`scoreCardArtifact`, `gradeCardOperation`, `gradeCardAnswer`) takes loader-returned cards and uses the schema's own types | yes |
| N8 | "moved here from `@objectstack/cli` … never released from the CLI" | yes: pure-rename commit; no scorer entry in the CLI CHANGELOG |
| N9–N13 | a closed 9-tag table (unscored counted nowhere), agent-action exposure (`ai.exposed`, `ai.requiresConfirmation`), the write-outcome grader, per-persona grading | yes |
| N14–N16 | the CLI's `MetadataEvalCase` relocation; no behaviour change, flag or export; no model call | yes |

The deletion loses no true user-facing statement: every still-true fact of the old note is restated in the new one.

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT at head `4dd3edc52bdfe115b3b86dce74a3b31df4450e4a`.**

1. **Shape.**
   - Line 1 is `Fixes #30291`. Body item 2 (`os lint --eval` reads cards) is cancelled by maintainer ruling D, verbatim 「同意 D」 (#30291, comment 6670490510).
   - `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in the body and the changeset.
   - The body was written by the seat from the dev's replacement (comment 6671781042).
   - The title is corrected in this stroke from `feat(cli)` to `feat(scenarios)`: the reviewer flagged that the CLI no longer ships the scorer.
2. **Size.** PR additions + deletions = **1806** (+1741/−65), the SKILL.md authority, under 3000. `dispatch-gates` reads 4324 because it counts with `--no-renames`; that tool defect is filed as #30718.
3. **Scope.** Inside the surface amended by the ruling, plus gate-forced files: `vitest.config.ts` source aliases, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and the type-only `corpus.ts` / `metadata-eval.ts` move that keeps the CLI's lint command out of the scenarios type-check program. All are accepted deviations. No `packages/spec` change; no public surface.
4. **Tests and gates.**
   - Dev side: 11 files / 163 tests in `@objectstack/scenarios`; the core security pin 4/4; CLI typecheck, build and lint tests 43/43; one ablation per moved module, each red then restored.
   - CI on this head: everything green except `Check Changeset` (see 5).
5. **DELIBERATE CORRECTION, confirmed** (landing-operations: for a PR that also changes code, a same-head contract-tier review PASS that judges the rewritten note sentence by sentence). The note is `.changeset/30290-scenario-scorer-port.md`, pending and unreleased, from merged PR #30332. What changed under it: this PR moves the scorer it announces out of `@objectstack/cli`. The judgement is the contract review above (PASS, same head). ⛔ The note is not restored: restoring it would publish a now-false CLI changelog line.
6. **Queueing with the designed red:** all three conditions of SKILL.md hold.
   1. The gate's own source says it is red by design on a pushed branch for this class: `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` — "this gate stays red either way, and staying red is what puts the decision in front of a person".
   2. `Check Changeset` runs in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, which triggers on `pull_request` only, never `merge_group`.
   3. This comment records the gate and the reason.
7. **Landing.** Ready, then auto-merge or merge queue through the relay in the next stroke.
8. **Out-of-scope findings.**
   - The `--no-renames` size count is filed as #30718.
   - Tag-name misalignment in the mid-tier cards: notes are posted on #30477–#30481 for `domain:devx#1`, and the epic files an add-rows card once the six land.
